Phase 1: Job Initiation

CarryOver.Jobs (Background Job)

Process Flow:

  1. Schedule Trigger: Runs Dec 31, 23:59 PM (plan year end)
  2. Plan Year Check: Query database for ended plan years
    SELECT * FROM PlanYear WHERE EndDate < GETDATE()
  3. Feature Flag Load: Check SplitJobPerformanceV2
    • Global flag: Enabled/Disabled
    • Per-employer flag: Overrides global setting
  4. Service Call: Invoke CarryoverDollarsDomainService
    CalculateForefeitAndCarryoverBalanceEOFYAllEmployersIdAsync( new ProcessCarryOverRequest { BatchSize = 1000, Concurrency = 10 } )

Phase 2: Domain Service Orchestration

Step 2.1: Fetch All Eligible Accounts

SELECT ra.ReimbursementAccountId, ra.MemberId, ra.EmployerId, ra.PlanType, ra.AvailableBalance, rp.PlanYearEndDate, rp.AllowCarryover FROM ReimbursementAccount ra INNER JOIN ReimbursementPlan rp ON ra.PlanId = rp.PlanId WHERE rp.PlanYearEndDate < GETDATE() AND ra.AvailableBalance > 0 AND rp.AllowCarryover = 1 AND ra.AccountStatus = 'Active'

Result: ~50,000 accounts retrieved

Step 2.2: Feature Flag Filtering

For each employer, check if V2 batch processing is enabled:

isEnabled = await GetIsEmployerCarryoverFeatureFlagEnabledAsync(employerId); if (!isEnabled) { // Skip employer's accounts (V1 fallback or disabled) excludedAccounts.AddRange( accounts.Where(a => a.EmployerId == employerId) ); }

Result: ~40,000 accounts (20% excluded via feature flags)

Step 2.3: Batch Splitting

var batches = enabledAccounts .Chunk(1000) // Split into batches of 1,000 .ToList(); // Total: 40 batches

Step 2.4: Parallel Processing (V2 Optimization)

var options = new ParallelOptions { MaxDegreeOfParallelism = 10 // 10 concurrent operations }; await Parallel.ForEachAsync(batches, options, async batch => { await ProcessBatchAsync(batch); });

Execution: 40 batches ÷ 10 concurrent = 4 waves (~4 minutes total)

Step 2.5: Pre-Fetch Claim Data (Performance Optimization)

var accountIds = batch.Select(a => a.ReimbursementAccountId); var claimData = await _context.Claims .Where(c => accountIds.Contains(c.ReimbursementAccountId)) .Where(c => c.ClaimStatus == "Pending") .GroupBy(c => c.ReimbursementAccountId) .Select(g => new { AccountId = g.Key, PendingAmount = g.Sum(c => c.ClaimAmount) }) .ToListAsync();

Performance Gain: 1,000 individual queries → 1 batch query (99% faster)

Phase 3: Account-Level Processing

Step 3.1: Load IRS Limits

var currentYear = account.PlanYearEndDate.Year; var irsLimits = await _context .GlobalContributionMaxByYear .Where(g => g.Year == currentYear) .ToDictionaryAsync(g => g.PlanType, g => g.MaxAmount); decimal IRSMaxForHSACarryover = irsLimits["HSA"]; // Expected: $4,300 (individual) // or $8,550 (family) for 2025

Step 3.2: Load Plan Rules

var rolloverSettings = await _context .RolloverSettings .Where(r => r.PlanId == account.PlanId) .FirstOrDefaultAsync(); // Contains: // - MaxCarryoverAmount (FSA: $640) // - GracePeriodMonths (0 or 2.5) // - AllowCarryover (true/false)

Step 3.3: Validation

ValidateReimbursementAccountAndPlanEligibleForRollover()

  • ✅ account.AccountStatus == "Active"
  • ✅ account.PlanYearEndDate < DateTime.Now
  • ✅ account.AvailableBalance > 0
  • ✅ rolloverSettings.AllowCarryover == true
  • ✅ No pending disputes/holds

Step 3.4: Calculate Carryover Amount

CalculateCarryoverAmountAllowedAtPlanYearEnd()

Plan Type Logic Example
FSA Math.Min(balance, 640m) $1,200 → $640 carryover, $560 forfeited
HSA return balance (100%) $3,500 → $3,500 carryover, $0 forfeited
HRA GetEmployerDefinedLimit() Varies by employer plan
Dependent Care FSA return 0m $2,000 → $0 carryover, $2,000 forfeited

Step 3.5: Calculate Forfeited Amount

decimal forfeitedAmount = accountBalance - carryoverAmount; // Examples: // FSA with $1,200 balance: // - Carryover: $640 // - Forfeited: $560 (returned to employer) // // HSA with $3,500 balance: // - Carryover: $3,500 (100%) // - Forfeited: $0 (employee-owned funds)

Phase 4: Database Persistence

Transaction-Protected Updates

using (var transaction = await _context.Database .BeginTransactionAsync(IsolationLevel.ReadCommitted)) { try { // All updates within transaction await UpdateReimbursementAccountBalance(); await InsertCarryoverTransferTracking(); await InsertBalanceChangeAudit(); await transaction.CommitAsync(); } catch (Exception ex) { await transaction.RollbackAsync(); throw; } }

Operations:

  1. Update ReimbursementAccount: Set new balance, carryover amount, last modified date
  2. Insert CarryoverTransferTracking: Audit trail (source→destination account, amounts)
  3. Insert BalanceChangeAudit: HIPAA compliance record (old/new balance, reason, timestamp)

Transaction Safety

  • ✅ ACID Compliance: All updates within database transaction
  • ✅ Optimistic Locking: WHERE AvailableBalance = @expectedOldBalance
  • ✅ Rollback on Error: try/catch with transaction.RollbackAsync()
  • ✅ Isolation Level: ReadCommitted (prevents dirty reads)

Phase 5: Event Publishing

NServiceBus Event Publishing

var balanceChangedEvent = new BalanceChangedEvent { ReimbursementAccountId = account.ReimbursementAccountId, MemberId = account.MemberId, OldBalance = accountBalance, NewBalance = accountBalance - forfeitedAmount, ChangeAmount = -forfeitedAmount, ChangeReason = "YEAR_END_CARRYOVER", CarryoverAmount = carryoverAmount, ForfeitedAmount = forfeitedAmount, TransactionId = transactionId, EventTimestamp = DateTime.UtcNow }; await _messageBus.PublishAsync(balanceChangedEvent);

Downstream Consumers:

Subscriber 1: StatementGenerationService

  • Triggers monthly statement generation
  • Includes carryover transaction in PDF

Subscriber 2: ReportingService

  • Updates data warehouse for BI reporting
  • Tracks year-end forfeiture revenue

Subscriber 3: AnalyticsService

  • Logs event for member behavior analysis
  • Tracks carryover utilization rates

Subscriber 4: NotificationService

  • Sends email to member confirming carryover
  • Example: "Your $640 has been carried over to 2026"

Batch Size 1 account 1,000 accounts 1000x
Concurrency 1 thread 10 threads 10x
DB Queries per Account 5 queries 0.005 queries (batch pre-fetch) 1000x
Total Time (50,000 accounts) 120-180 min 15-20 min 85% faster

Batch Processing Timeline (V2)

50,000 accounts ÷ 1,000 per batch = 50 batches 50 batches ÷ 10 concurrent = 5 waves Wave 1: Batches 1-10 (0-4 min) ███████████ Wave 2: Batches 11-20 (4-8 min) ███████████ Wave 3: Batches 21-30 (8-12 min) ███████████ Wave 4: Batches 31-40 (12-16 min) ███████████ Wave 5: Batches 41-50 (16-20 min) ███████████ Total: 15-20 minutes (vs. 2-3 hours in V1)

Key Entities in Workflow

1. ReimbursementAccount

class ReimbursementAccount { Guid ReimbursementAccountId; Guid MemberId; Guid EmployerId; string PlanType; // FSA, HSA, HRA decimal AvailableBalance; decimal CarriedOverBalance; DateTime PlanYearEndDate; string AccountStatus; }

2. CarryoverTransferTracking

class CarryoverTransferTracking { Guid CarryoverTransferTrackingId; Guid SourceAccountId; // 2025 Guid DestAccountId; // 2026 decimal CarryoverAmount; decimal ForfeitedAmount; Guid TransactionId; DateTime ProcessedDate; string ProcessedBy; }

3. RolloverSettings

class RolloverSettings { Guid RolloverSettingsId; Guid PlanId; decimal? MaxCarryoverAmount; // $640 int? GracePeriodMonths; // 0 or 2.5 bool AllowCarryover; }

4. GlobalContributionMaxByYear

class GlobalContributionMaxByYear { int Year; // 2025 string PlanType; // FSA, HSA decimal MaxContributionAmount; // $3,200 decimal MaxCarryoverAmount; // $640 DateTime EffectiveDate; }
